findings.summary: Edges are labelled with bare numbers only, so a reader must cross-reference the 17-entry key beneath the panels to learn any relationship's type and its live ITER count; the relationship name never sits beside the edge it names. The two-hop read slows the figure at every edge, and the label on the top-right FacilitySignal-SignalContextLink edge (key entry 9, HAS_PLANT_CONTEXT 225) is hard to resolve as a digit at display size.

The bottom third of the image is a 17-row inventory of relationship name plus live count, set as two ragged, unaligned column blocks rather than an aligned table. That name/count inventory is naturally tabular, and its counts (90,314 against 225 against 7) are hard to compare in the current ragged form.

Key entry 17 reads as a migration sentence ('PlantContextDocument to Document: 7 nodes migrate') where the other 16 entries are a relationship type and a count. A reader using the key as a lookup gets prose for the one entry, and the dashed 17 edge in the right panel cannot be matched to a relationship name the way the others can.

rubric_items.contrast: All text clears its background: dark node labels and counts on white boxes, blue proposal labels and the blue ArchiveFieldCode box legible on white, and the key text dark enough to read at display size.
rubric_items.data_ink: The data carry the weight: node boxes, class names and live counts are the substance; there is no grid, gradient or decorative fill competing with the data.
rubric_items.decoration: No gradient, background fill, drop shadow or decorative styling; plain boxes and lines on white, which is what the plot style asks for.
rubric_items.label_collision: No clipped or overlapping labels in the rendered PNG: the closest pair (edge boxes 15 and 1 near ControlNode) still has a visible gap, and no label sits on top of the plotted data.
rubric_items.legibility: Readable at a glance for the class map: each node box carries its name and live count, and the two panels (classes reached from a signal, and the document and field-code side) are clearly separated. One defect: edges carry bare numbers, so a reader must jump to the key beneath to learn a relationship's name and count, and the top-right edge label does not resolve clearly as a digit at display size.
rubric_items.table_form: The top two-thirds is a node-link diagram, which is the right form for topology, but the bottom third is a 17-row relationship inventory (name plus count) set as two ragged column blocks rather than an aligned table. That portion is naturally tabular.
